carla (ml-eng): Quick question — before we finalize the RFC: can we get a clean mapping of runtime dependencies for per-request quant switching? Need to know which teams own what and where the compatibility surface is.

 dmitri (runtime): Short answer: it's split across 3 surfaces — model artifact (quant metadata), runtime kernel selection, and routing/serving policy. Need to document interface contracts.

 ben (infra): +1. Also include storage format/manifest changes (S3 layout) and cache key semantics. If model metadata changes, cache invalidation triggers.

 carla (ml-eng): Agreed. I'm mainly worried about quality regressions when we fallback across precision lanes. We need telemetry hooks to measure delta per-request.

 alice (sre): For SLAs we can't have silent quality shifts. Propose per-route degradation metric: baseline perplexity/accuracy delta + user-visible error rate. If delta > threshold, auto-rollback route. :warning: 

 dmitri (runtime): Implementation sketch:
```
model.tar
  model.bin
  quant_meta.json  # per-layer scales, format, fallback profile ids
  version.txt
```
Runtime loads quant_meta, computes kernel plan, exposes plan_id in request traces.

 carla (ml-eng): plan_id is perfect. ML team will add eval-set signatures to quant_meta so we can compute quality escrows at rollout time.

 dmitri (runtime): Need to define plan_id stability rules. If quant_meta changes but model weights same, plan_id changes -> cache miss. Is that acceptable?

 ben (infra): We can namespace caches by model:version:plan_id. Plan_id churn will increase S3 GETs and redis evictions. Ops cost tradeoff.

 alice (sre): What about on-the-fly re-quantization? Dangerous for SLA. Recommend disallow by default; allow as opt-in with canary periods and manual approvals.

 carla (ml-eng): Action items:
- ML: add eval signatures + fallback profile list to quant_meta (carla)
- Runtime: define plan_id hashing + backwards-compat rule (dmitri)
- Infra: simulate cache churn cost for plan_id churn scenarios (ben)
- SRE: define degradation thresholds and rollback automation (alice)

 dmitri (runtime): Also one design choice: do we expose precision hints in the public API (developers choose FP8/INT8) or keep it internal with a "cost_profile" selector?

 carla (ml-eng): Prefer internal only. External API increases support surface; keep it behind model profiles and runtime selectors. :thumbsup: 

 ben (infra): We must document billing implications. If a request falls back from FP8 to fp16, billing should reflect consumed tokens + allocation tier.

 ops-bot: reminder — meeting scheduled: quant-runtime sync, Thu 15:00 PT. Agenda: plan_id hashing + telemetry schema.

 carla (ml-eng): Thanks. I'll draft a small followup RFC appendix with eval hooks and a sample quant_meta schema.

 alice (sre): One more: trace-level tag suggestion: `precision_lane`, `plan_id`, `fallback_reason`, `quality_score_delta` — include in traces and metrics.

 dmitri (runtime): Noted. Will add to the telemetry PR. End.
